mission: Turn each row of counts into a probability distribution with one broadcast division. A row of all zeros stays all zeros instead of becoming NaN.
taskDescription: Implement `row_normalize(counts)`. Divide every row by its own sum so each row sums to 1. A row whose sum is 0 must come back as all zeros. Return a list of lists.
constraints: No Python loop over rows: use `sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)` and broadcasting.
A zero row returns zeros, never NaN.
Return `.tolist()`, not an array.

hints.small: Row sums have shape (n, 1) when you pass keepdims=True, and (n, 1) broadcasts against (n, d).
hints.strong: Replace zero sums with 1 before dividing: the zero row divided by 1 is still zeros.
hints.concept: Broadcasting stretches a size-1 axis to match the other array without copying data.

mission: Use a boolean mask and np.where to replace values more than k standard deviations from their column mean, the kind of cleaning step that runs before training on sensor data.
taskDescription: Implement `replace_outliers(X, k)`. For each column compute its mean and population standard deviation (ddof=0). Any value with `abs(x - mean) > k * std` is replaced by that column's mean. Means and stds come from the original data. Return a list of lists.
constraints: Use column statistics computed once, before any replacement.
A column with std 0 has no outliers.
Strictly greater than k * std counts as an outlier; equal does not.

hints.small: mean and std with axis=0 give one value per column, shape (d,).
hints.strong: mask = np.abs(X - mean) > k * std; then np.where(mask, mean, X). Broadcasting lines the (d,) vectors up with each row.
hints.concept: A z-score threshold is the simplest outlier rule; it assumes roughly normal columns.

hints.small: Sum first, then divide by the count per segment. np.bincount gives the counts.
hints.strong: np.add.at(sums, ids, values) adds every row, even when ids repeat. counts = np.bincount(ids, minlength=num_segments).
hints.concept: Scatter-add is how graph neural networks aggregate messages from neighbours.
